standards.name: WheatPhenotype ontology
standards.abstract: The WheatPhenotype ontology is a domain ontology developed to represent phenotype and marker–trait information described in the scientific literature about wheat (Triticum aestivum). The source material describes using this ontology as part of an automated information-extraction pipeline applied to scientific papers (text modality) to recover links between molecular markers, genes, and agronomically relevant traits (for example, grain number or disease resistance). The ontology and associated knowledge model were developed by the paper's authors and presented in a Springer CCIS conference volume; the extracted information was evaluated and integrated into the online semantic search engine AlvisIR WheatMarker.

classification.rationale: The source material is prose describing an ontology and its intended use in an information-extraction workflow. It does not present a field-level metadata table or a sequential DAG of stages; instead it describes goals, scope, and usage recommendations — a principles-style document.

principles.principle: Use an ontology (WheatPhenotype) as the knowledge model for extracting phenotype/marker information from literature.
principles.evidence: relying on a knowledge model of the target information and on the WheatPhenotype ontology that we developed for this purpose.

principles.principle: Automate extraction of marker/trait information from scientific papers (text modality).
principles.evidence: Here, we present a method aiming at automatically extract this information from the scientific literature

principles.principle: Target agronomically relevant trait information, including links between molecular markers, genes, and traits such as grain number or disease resistance.
principles.evidence: The recent advent of genomic tools contributed to improve the discovery of linkage between molecular markers and genes that are involved in the control of traits of agronomical interest such as grain number or disease resistance.

principles.principle: Address the gap that much marker–trait information appears in papers but is rarely available in databases.
principles.evidence: This information is mostly published as scientific papers but rarely available in databases.

principles.principle: Integrate and evaluate extracted information in a semantic search platform (AlvisIR WheatMarker).
principles.evidence: The information extraction results were evaluated and integrated into the on-line semantic search engine AlvisIR WheatMarker.

standards.notes: Source is a conference chapter abstract (MTSR 2014, Communications in Computer and Information Science) by Nédellec et al.; available as Springer CCIS content. The seed material is limited to an abstract/preview so detailed ontology terms and field-level structure were not present in the provided text.
